name: ci.yml
purpose: The gate workflow: fourteen jobs, ordered cheapest-first, run on every push to main/claude/** and every PR into main; every job is a hard failure with no warning suppressed.
key_contracts: sbom: cargo cyclonedx --format json --all, uploaded as artifact
frontend-portal: npm ci, tokens:check, tsc --noEmit, lint, build, playwright (frontend/portal)
trivy: trivy fs --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --exit-code 1 --ignore-unfixed over the whole tree
infrastructure: terraform fmt/validate, tfvars parse, GitOps manifest parse, plan-the-gates, check-terraform-providers.sh
production_evidence: GitHub-dispatched on push/pull_request (.github/workflows/ci.yml:9-11); deploy.yml's gate job requires this workflow's conclusion == success for the commit before any image is built or shipped (deploy.yml on: workflow_run triggers off ci).
io_and_state: GitHub-hosted runners; cargo-audit and cargo-deny reach the network for the advisory database; trivy downloads its own apt repo key; no state persisted beyond the SBOM artifact (90-day retention) and the ephemeral runner.
status_reason: Every job maps 1:1 to a Makefile target per the file's own header comment and both are exercised routinely per commit history.
gaps_observed: deploy.yml only runs automatically off ci's workflow_run on branch "main" (deploy.yml:44-56) — but the current default branch history note in that same file records the branch filter was blank for a period and the automatic path was unreachable; nothing in ci.yml re-verifies that its own branch list still matches the repository's actual default branch.

ci.yml:393-399 secrets job runs ./scripts/check-secrets.sh with fetch-depth 0 but the script itself (scripts/check-secrets.sh) only greps the working tree, not history, despite the fetch-depth:0 checkout suggesting history scanning was intended.

name: deploy.yml
purpose: Builds, signs, attests and ships the catalogue of images, then replaces execution-node instances under their rolling policy. Runs automatically after ci succeeds on main, or by manual dispatch choosing dev/test/stage/prod.
key_contracts: gate job: refuses prod unless workflow_dispatch; validates TARGET_ENVIRONMENT/DEPLOY_SHA charset before use; confirms the triggering ci run is this repo's own and succeeded for the exact commit
images job: derive-identity-from-tfvars, keyless auth, check-if-registry-already-holds-commit, build, scan, push, sign
deploy job: derive-identity-from-tfvars, keyless auth, read-the-catalogue, record-attested-digests, replace-every-execution-node-under-its-groups-rolling-policy
production_evidence: Dispatches automatically after ci succeeds on main (deploy.yml:44-56) or manually; the deploy job's last step provisions execution nodes, but every environment's execution_nodes = {} (per infrastructure tfvars), so the rolling-replace step has nothing to iterate in any currently-configured environment.
io_and_state: Authenticates via Workload Identity Federation (no downloaded keys); pushes/signs images in Artifact Registry; reads Terraform tfvars for identity; no local state written by the workflow itself.
status_reason: Image build/sign/attest path is exercised; the execution-node rollout step has no nodes to roll in any environment because execution_nodes = {} everywhere.
gaps_observed: deploy.yml:150 'replace every execution node under its group's rolling policy' iterates infrastructure execution-node groups, but every environment's tfvars sets execution_nodes = {} (per docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md and .claude/rules/domains/observability.md), so this step is a no-op wherever it runs today.

name: image.yml
purpose: Manual-dispatch-only workflow that bakes the execution-node boot image (a GCE machine image) from attested pipeline artifacts, never from a push, so an image bake is always a deliberate, billed act.
key_contracts: bake job, dispatch inputs: environment (dev/test/stage), machine_type, base_image (full self-link, no family), commit

steps: refuse-what-this-workflow-must-never-do, check-inputs, verify-source-files-are-reviewed, derive-identity, keyless-auth, install crane, verify-artifacts-were-attested, extract-binaries, stage-pinned-ops-agent, build-payload, create/wait/retire builder VM, create-image, release-builder-disk
production_evidence: Manual workflow_dispatch only (image.yml:106); ADR 0035 authorises one node in dev and per .claude rules docs no execution node has ever been baked/deployed.
io_and_state: Creates and destroys a transient GCE builder VM; writes a GCE machine image; reads attested container images from Artifact Registry by digest.
status_reason: The workflow exists and is structurally complete but ADR 0035 notes it has never been applied; no execution node exists in any environment to consume the baked image.
gaps_observed: The whole workflow is 'never yet applied' per top-level CLAUDE.md: 'one Compute Engine execution node per region (ADR 0024, never yet applied)'.

name: infra.yml
purpose: The single Terraform operations workflow: one job, one action input selecting among plan/up/apps/suspend/down/teardown/force-unlock/diagnose, manually dispatched against dev/test/stage only (prod is not an option — it is applied only via scripts/bootstrap-deploy.sh by a person).
key_contracts: terraform job, action=plan: read-only plan against provided var-files
action=up: terraform apply + bootstrap GitOps controllers (Argo CD, Config Connector, cert-manager, Kargo) + console IAP gate
action=apps: apply the Argo CD Application/Kargo chain onto an existing control plane, re-runnable alone
action=suspend / down / teardown: destroy control-plane cluster / execution nodes (no-op today) / full environment teardown sparing the running identity
action=force-unlock: release a stuck state lock by id
action=diagnose: read-only Cloud Run revision/condition/log dump
production_evidence: dev has been applied via this workflow's 'up' action (docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md records run 52 applying 238 Terraform-managed resources) and later suspended by ADR 0093 because the Argo CD image fails the vendor scan gate.
io_and_state: Applies/destroys real GCP resources (Cloud Run, KMS, IAM, buckets, GKE Autopilot control-plane cluster) via Workload Identity Federation; no service-account keys.
status_reason: The 'up' path was applied in dev but its bootstrap step failed (docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md: run 52 concludes 'failure' at the bootstrap step following a clean apply) because the GitOps controllers' images fail the vendor.yml Trivy scan gate; the environment is now suspended (ADR 0093).
gaps_observed: infra.yml action=up's GitOps bootstrap step depends on vendor.yml successfully mirroring Argo CD's image, which vendor.yml refuses on CVE-2025-68121 with no available upstream fix (docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md 'Argo CD fails the scan gate' row) — so 'up' cannot currently complete a working control plane in any environment.
evidence: docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md (Argo CD fails the scan gate row)

name: vendor.yml
purpose: Mirrors a fixed list of upstream vendor images (infrastructure/egress/vendored-images.txt) into the project's own Artifact Registry, verifying, scanning and attesting each — automatically for dev on a push to the vendored-images list, manually for test/stage/prod.
key_contracts: mirror job: derive-identity, keyless-auth, install crane+trivy, 'mirror, verify, scan, attest' (per-image loop), 'derive, scan and attest the patched images', 'the gate's verdict' (final pass/fail summarising every image)
production_evidence: Runs automatically on push to main touching infrastructure/egress/vendored-images.txt (vendor.yml:32-39); its blocking severity-CRITICAL gate currently refuses the Argo CD image, which cascades to block cert-manager's images in the same fail-fast loop (docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md).
io_and_state: Pulls from public registries (quay.io etc.), pushes to project Artifact Registry, writes Binary Authorization attestations.
status_reason: Currently fails on CVE-2025-68121 in Argo CD's bundled kustomize/git-lfs with no fixed upstream version available; because the loop runs under set -euo pipefail, the failure stops cert-manager's images from mirroring too, per docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md's own measurement.
gaps_observed: Blocked entirely on an upstream fix; docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md explicitly says 'Do not clear with a scanner exception, an .trivyignore, or a per-image acknowledgement'.
evidence: docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md (Argo CD fails the scan gate row)

name: Makefile
purpose: The local counterpart of every ci.yml job, ordered cheapest-first, so a green `make` locally should not be surprised by CI; deliberately carries no `apply`/deploy target.
key_contracts: check (default): fmt-check lint test deps secrets
all: check build audit deny sbom infra
fmt/fmt-check, lint, test, count, build/release, e2e, acceptance, doc
help: prints every target's one-line description
production_evidence: Local developer/agent entry point; ci.yml runs the underlying commands directly rather than shelling out to `make` (confirmed identical commands, e.g. ci.yml test job vs Makefile `test` target).
io_and_state: Delegates to cargo/terraform/npm subprocesses; no state of its own.
status_reason: Every target has a 1:1 ci.yml counterpart per its own header, with one drift: `make test` omits --no-fail-fast (present in ci.yml's test job and in `make count`/count-tests.sh).
gaps_observed: Makefile:54-55 `test:` target runs `cargo test --workspace --all-features` without --no-fail-fast, while ci.yml's test job (ci.yml:79) and top-level CLAUDE.md's documented command both use --no-fail-fast; a local `make test` run can therefore abort at the first failing binary and under-report, exactly the failure mode the file's own `count` target and its comment (Makefile:57-62) warn about.

name: check-dependencies.sh
purpose: Enforces the two-dependency policy (ADR 0002/0009) by diffing every non-qip package name in backend/Cargo.lock against a hardcoded 11-name PERMITTED allowlist (serde/serde_json plus their transitive proc-macro closure).
key_contracts: exit 1 on any violation, exit 0 with a count on success
production_evidence: Called from ci.yml's dependency-policy job (ci.yml:97-108), Makefile's `deps` target, and .claude/settings.json's allowlisted Bash commands.
io_and_state: Reads backend/Cargo.lock only; no writes, no network.
status_reason: Runs on every CI push and locally via `make deps`; fails closed if the lockfile is missing.
gaps_observed: PERMITTED list (scripts/check-dependencies.sh:19-35) is hand-maintained text, duplicated in intent by backend/deny.toml's [bans] allowlist; the two are asserted to agree only by docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md prose, not by a shared source.

name: check-secrets.sh
purpose: Greps the tracked working tree (git grep) for private-key headers, AWS/Google/GitHub/Hugging Face credential shapes, and key=value secret assignments, excluding target/, Cargo.lock, itself, and any tests/ directory.
production_evidence: Called from ci.yml's secrets job (ci.yml:393-399, with fetch-depth 0) and Makefile's `secrets` target; also allowlisted in .claude/settings.json.
io_and_state: git grep over the working tree only; no network, no writes.
status_reason: Deliberately narrow patterns per its own header comment to avoid alert fatigue; its own module doc says the acceptance suite's security.rs carries a matching copy of the vendor-prefix patterns so the two cannot silently drift apart.
gaps_observed: git grep with fetch-depth:0 in CI still only scans the current tree, not history, despite the full-history checkout — history scanning is not implemented here.

name: check-manifests.py
purpose: Parses every GitOps/Kubernetes YAML manifest under infrastructure/ with a real YAML parser and refuses one that does not parse, closing a gap where every prior gate (gitops.rs, console_route.rs, terraform fmt) only read manifests as text.
key_contracts: exit non-zero naming the file and the parser's own diagnostic
production_evidence: Called from ci.yml's infrastructure job ('the GitOps manifests parse' step) and Makefile's tf-manifests target, part of the `infra` target.
io_and_state: Reads infrastructure/ YAML files only.
status_reason: Added after a real incident (an unquoted colon in a comment broke `kustomize build` ten minutes into an infra.yml apps dispatch) per its own module docstring.

name: check-terraform-providers.sh
purpose: Statically checks that every provider a Terraform module references (e.g. google-beta) is declared in that module's required_providers block, catching a class of error `terraform validate` misses because validate does not need provider credentials.
key_contracts: static scan, no terraform init/credentials needed
exit non-zero naming the module and missing provider
production_evidence: Called from ci.yml's infrastructure job ('provider declarations' step) and allowlisted directly in .claude/settings.json.
io_and_state: Reads infrastructure/terraform/**/*.tf only.
status_reason: Written after modules/ai used google-beta undeclared and only a real plan (needing credentials) caught it, per its own header.
gaps_observed: Explicitly does not catch a resource type that exists only in a non-default provider without an explicit provider= argument, per its own header comment — a stated, accepted limitation.

name: count-tests.sh
purpose: Runs the whole workspace test suite with --no-fail-fast and sums both the 'passed' and 'failed' columns from cargo's own output (rather than only the passed column), because a failed test binary prints nothing summable into a naive passed-only tally.
production_evidence: Makefile's `count` target; allowlisted in .claude/settings.json.
io_and_state: Runs the full backend test suite (spawns cargo, writes to a temp file it cleans up on exit).
status_reason: Exists specifically because summing only 'test result: ok. N passed' lines under-reports silently when a binary fails outright, per its own header.

name: worker-capacity.sh
purpose: Reports (does not gate) the actual concurrency this machine can sustain for the agent-orchestration harness — CPU, memory and disk ceilings — against a fixed 8/16/32/64/100 policy ladder, so the operating point is measured rather than aspirational.
key_contracts: prints cpu/mem/disk ceilings and the binding constraint
production_evidence: Operator/orchestrator tooling, not part of the platform's own deployable binaries.
io_and_state: Reads /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/meminfo, df of cwd; no writes.
status_reason: Advisory-only script for the delivery/orchestration harness, not a CI gate.

name: audit-dead-code.py
purpose: Finds pub items in src/ whose name is referenced nowhere outside their own declaration (workspace-wide name matching), producing a CANDIDATE list for a human to sort into genuine dead code, deliberate public API, or an unwired control — the third being the dangerous one (its own example: MaxExpectedShortfall).
key_contracts: outputs a candidate list, not a defect list
production_evidence: Developer/audit tooling; not invoked by any CI job found in .github/workflows/ or the Makefile.
io_and_state: Reads backend/crates/**/src/**/*.rs; no writes.
status_reason: Not wired into ci.yml or the Makefile — a manually-invoked audit aid; its own docstring says matching is by name workspace-wide, which deliberately under-reports on short/common names.
gaps_observed: Not called from any CI job or Makefile target found (grep of both turned up nothing referencing this script by name).

name: audit-register.py
purpose: Re-runs docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md's own cited evidence commands and reports which claims have gone stale, specifically catching two classes: an 'EMPTINESS' claim (a command asserted to return nothing that now returns something) and an 'ONLY-TESTS' claim (a command asserted to hit only test code that now hits src/ after that file's last #[cfg(test)] marker).
key_contracts: parses DELIVERY-STATUS.md rows for cited commands
ONLY-TESTS check (position-based: hit after last top-level #[cfg(test)] in a src file counts as production)
production_evidence: Documentation/register audit tooling; written after 4 false claims (understating the platform) were found by hand on 2026-09-16.
io_and_state: Reads docs/DELIVERY-STATUS.md and re-executes its embedded shell/grep commands against the working tree; no writes observed in the header.
status_reason: Purpose-built register-integrity tool; not confirmed wired into ci.yml or the Makefile from the workflow/Makefile scan performed.
gaps_observed: Not found referenced in .github/workflows/*.yml or the Makefile — appears to be run manually/by an agent lane rather than gated in CI.

name: terraform-undeletable.py
purpose: Shared parser for the one list of Google resources Terraform cannot delete-and-recreate cleanly: 'addresses' (what teardown removes from state) and 'imports' (which of a plan's creates would collide with something teardown left behind), used to keep infra.yml's teardown and up actions from disagreeing about that list, after a real incident where they did.
production_evidence: Invoked from infra.yml's teardown/up steps per its own module docstring (the two callers share this one parse); referenced by name in infra.yml around the 'reclaim what the teardown left standing' step.
io_and_state: Parses Terraform module source files and a plan JSON; performs no Google API calls itself (the docstring is explicit: 'this file resolves nothing against Google and imports nothing').
status_reason: Directly motivated by a real incident: run 44 planned to create 184 resources against a project still holding 9 crypto keys, a keyring and 5 buckets from an aborted teardown.

name: bootstrap-deploy.sh
purpose: The one-command first deployment / prod deployment path: enables project APIs, creates the bootstrap service account (impersonated, no downloaded key), creates the Terraform state bucket, runs terraform init+apply (always showing the plan, never auto-approving), grants scoped object-delete on the state bucket, and seeds generated secrets.
production_evidence: Named in the Makefile's help text and docs/operations/deployment-path.md as the only path for a first apply and for prod (Makefile:174-176 comment: 'scripts/bootstrap-deploy.sh for the first apply and for prod').
io_and_state: Applies real GCP resources; writes to Secret Manager; requires the caller's own gcloud identity (Cloud Shell or local).
status_reason: Deliberately outside CI/Makefile automation — a person-run script by design, per the Makefile's own comment that an `apply` Makefile target would be 'exactly the wrong affordance'.

name: deploy-frontends.sh
purpose: Builds and deploys the portal (first) and landing (second, inlining the portal's live URL at build time) to Cloud Run by digest, signing each with the pipeline's own attestor/key version and reading back the routed revision to confirm it serves those exact bytes.
production_evidence: Operator-run script (uses the caller's own gcloud login), not dispatched by any workflow found in .github/workflows/.
io_and_state: gcloud builds submit, Cloud Run deploy, Secret Manager (session secret, generated once, never printed).
status_reason: A manual operator path for the two Next.js frontends, parallel to but not gated by ci.yml/deploy.yml, which only handle the Rust backend images.

name: model-gateway.mjs
purpose: A zero-dependency Node worker-model gateway that routes bounded, low-risk agent-orchestration tasks to an external LLM provider, screening every payload for credential-shaped content and refusing (not scrubbing) the call if any is found; explicitly dev tooling that no backend/ or frontend/ crate may import.
key_contracts: credential screening refuses rather than scrubs
production_evidence: Explicitly excluded by its own doc comment: 'Nothing in backend/crates/ or frontend/packages/ may import it, and the platform does not depend on it existing.'
io_and_state: Node built-in fetch to an external model provider; reads an API key from a _FILE-indirected path.
status_reason: Delivery/orchestration tooling by design, structurally isolated from the platform's own dependency graph.

name: model-gateway.test.mjs
purpose: Test coverage for model-gateway.mjs's credential screening and fail-closed configuration behaviour.
production_evidence: Test file for a dev-tooling script; not part of the platform's own test suites.
io_and_state: n/a
status_reason: Not enumerated by #[test] (JS test file); size (139 lines) suggests meaningful coverage but was not read in full for this pass.
gaps_observed: Not confirmed wired into ci.yml or a package.json test script during this pass — worth checking separately.

name: venue-signup
purpose: An operator-machine browser-automation job that performs a venue's signup form under the company's identity after a named operator has approved that venue's terms, refusing every step that must remain a person's act (captchas, identity documents, verification codes, any field a reviewed recipe does not list); explicitly dev tooling backend/ and frontend/ never import.
key_contracts: signup.mjs (1053 lines): main job, origin-matching, ambiguous-selector refusal, credential-blanked screenshot on hand-back
recipes/alpaca.json, recipes/kalshi.json: reviewed per-venue field recipes
production_evidence: Explicitly excluded per its own doc comment, same pattern as model-gateway.mjs: 'nothing in backend/ or frontend/ imports it and the platform does not depend on it existing.'
io_and_state: Drives a real browser against a live venue signup page; writes a credential-blanked screenshot on any hand-back.
status_reason: Purpose-built operator tooling for venue onboarding, structurally separate from the trading platform per its own doc comment.

name: claude-agents
purpose: Thirteen role-scoped subagent definitions (frontmatter: name, description, allowed tools) used by the orchestration workflow to split delivery work by specialty; each is a short markdown mission statement, not executable code.
production_evidence: Harness-level configuration for Claude Code's own agent-dispatch, not part of the platform's deployable binaries.
io_and_state: None; static markdown read by the harness.
status_reason: documentation.rs's the_documented_agent_count_matches_the_roster asserts the docs count matches this roster, per its test name found in the acceptance suite.
gaps_observed: code-reviewer and security-engineer both explicitly withhold Write/Edit tools (read-only review by design) — consistent with each agent's description saying it 'must not review its own implementation'.

name: claude-skills
purpose: Eight ~36-line skill playbooks (Trigger/Outcome plus a checklist) that standardise how the harness performs architecture-review, documentation-update, implement-slice, incident-diagnosis, release-readiness, security-review, test-change and vision-to-plan.
production_evidence: Harness-level, invoked via the Skill tool by name; not part of the platform's deployable binaries.
io_and_state: None.
status_reason: Each file is short and uniformly shaped (Trigger/Outcome), all 8 confirmed present and non-empty (291 total lines across 8 files).

name: claude-hooks
purpose: Two Python PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks plus their own regression-test runner: guard-dangerous-command.py blocks a fixed list of destructive shell patterns (force push, rm -rf outside repo, terraform destroy/-auto-approve, gcloud/gsutil/kubectl deletes, destructive SQL) before Bash executes them; format-rust-after-edit.py runs rustfmt on any .rs file after Write/Edit and never blocks on failure.
key_contracts: guard-dangerous-command.py: RULES list of (needle-tuple, description, alternative); strip_heredocs() so a heredoc merely documenting a dangerous command is not itself blocked; exit 2 blocks, exit 0 allows
format-rust-after-edit.py: rustfmt --edition 2024 on the edited path; always exit 0
test_hooks.py: 17 table-driven GUARD_CASES plus malformed-payload and formatter-safety checks, run via `python3 .claude/hooks/test_hooks.py`
production_evidence: Wired directly in .claude/settings.json's hooks.PreToolUse (matcher Bash) and hooks.PostToolUse (matcher Edit|Write), so every Bash call and every file edit in this harness passes through them.
io_and_state: guard reads the pending tool_input JSON from stdin; formatter shells out to rustfmt on the edited file; neither performs network I/O.

notable: test_hooks.py: 17 GUARD_CASES table (allow+block), 4 malformed-payload cases, 3 formatter-never-blocks cases — run as a standalone script, not via #[test] or pytest discovery

status_reason: Both hooks document specific prior failures they were rewritten to fix (a heredoc quoting a dangerous command was wrongly blocked; an earlier shell version of the guard had a quoting bug that blocked every command), and test_hooks.py exercises both allow and block cases per its own stated principle that 'a guard that refuses everything is not secure, it is broken'.
gaps_observed: .claude/rules/01-security-and-safety.md's own prose still names the file 'guard-dangerous-command.sh' (Destructive operations section) while the actual, current implementation on disk is guard-dangerous-command.py — the rules doc has not been updated for the Python rewrite the hook's own docstring describes.

name: claude-rules
purpose: The working agreement's normative rule tree: four root governance files (enterprise-governance, security-and-safety, change-management, product-direction) imported by CLAUDE.md via @-includes, plus architecture/ (boundaries, testing-strategy) and domains/ (core-rust, frontend, data-and-streaming, risk-and-execution, observability, infrastructure).
key_contracts: 01-security-and-safety.md: the three paper-trading layers, secrets handling, destructive-op guard, untrusted-content rule
02-change-management.md: branch/commit rules, PR rules, Definition-of-Done gate table, test rules (incl. mutation verification), production rules
10-product-direction.md: standing product decisions and mandatory architecture concerns
production_evidence: Loaded into every Claude Code session's system context via CLAUDE.md @-includes; not code, has no runtime caller.
io_and_state: None; static markdown.
status_reason: The observability.md and architecture/00-boundaries.md files are unusually self-correcting: both carry dated, superseded-in-place corrections of their own prior wrong figures (e.g. ADR count, acceptance-suite count, metrics-recording-site count) rather than restating a number, specifically to avoid the drift pattern this record documents elsewhere.
gaps_observed: domains/observability.md is exceptionally long and includes multiple explicit 'this file was wrong until <date>' corrections about metric-recording-site counts, alert-policy counts and ADR references — the file itself states it should not be trusted for a bare figure and instructs the reader to run the cited grep/awk command instead.
01-security-and-safety.md names the hook file as guard-dangerous-command.sh; the actual file is guard-dangerous-command.py (see claude-hooks record).

name: claude-settings
purpose: The harness's permission policy for this repository: an allowlist of safe read-only/build commands (cargo build/check/clippy/fmt/test/tree, make, the check-*.sh scripts, terraform fmt/validate/plan, npm lint/build/test, git status/diff/log/add/commit, rg/ls/cat/head/tail/wc/find), an ask-list for higher-risk commands (git push, gcloud, gsutil, kubectl, terraform apply, npm install, cargo add/remove), a deny-list for credential/state-file reads, and the PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook wiring.
production_evidence: Read by the Claude Code harness itself at session start; not part of the deployed platform.
io_and_state: None; static JSON.
status_reason: deny-list matches the specific paths .claude/rules/01-security-and-safety.md names ('~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config/gcloud'), so the two are consistent as of this read.

name: acceptance.rs
purpose: The end-to-end acceptance scenario: one test walks a synthetic market observation through all seven stages to a reviewed thesis, checked proposal, risk-gated order and exact attribution; the rest assert properties that only hold once every crate is wired together (paper-boundary refusal, halt propagation, determinism, event-log hash-chain survival).
production_evidence: Cross-cutting acceptance test file; run via `cargo test -p qip-acceptance` / `make acceptance`, never called from a deployable binary itself — its purpose is to assert properties of production code assembled together.
io_and_state: In-process only: constructs real Platform/Cell instances against fixture data and an in-memory/temp-file event log; no live network or venue calls.
status_reason: Present in the workspace test tree; gated by ci.yml's `test` job (cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast) and `make acceptance`.

name: adversary.rs
purpose: Blueprint §15.2's AdversaryProfiles slot, proven through a real Platform driven through real fills: the counterfactual twin measures a venue filling the desk badly, the finding lands in the hash-chained log, and — the load-bearing claim — producing that finding moves nothing (ADR 0062: a venue is withdrawn on feasibility evidence and on nothing else, never on the twin's fill-error estimate).
production_evidence: Cross-cutting acceptance test file; run via `cargo test -p qip-acceptance` / `make acceptance`, never called from a deployable binary itself — its purpose is to assert properties of production code assembled together.
io_and_state: In-process only: constructs real Platform/Cell instances against fixture data and an in-memory/temp-file event log; no live network or venue calls.
status_reason: Present in the workspace test tree; gated by ci.yml's `test` job (cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast) and `make acceptance`.
gaps_observed: §15.2's twelfth AdversaryProfiles slot has 'been declared and unproduced since the payload was written' per this file's own module doc.

name: api_boundary.rs
purpose: Proves the application layer (qip-api/qip-web) is a thin interface, not a second domain: no execution/venue/capital/edge crate dependency, no order/transfer/envelope construction, money held only as text handed in and never as an owned numeric field, and every mutating route is enumerated with the single typed intent it raises.
production_evidence: Cross-cutting acceptance test file; run via `cargo test -p qip-acceptance` / `make acceptance`, never called from a deployable binary itself — its purpose is to assert properties of production code assembled together.
io_and_state: In-process only: constructs real Platform/Cell instances against fixture data and an in-memory/temp-file event log; no live network or venue calls.
status_reason: Present in the workspace test tree; gated by ci.yml's `test` job (cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast) and `make acceptance`.

name: truth_loop.rs
purpose: The Data Truth Loop (source event → state, 7 stages) that every later loop reads from: both bitemporal timestamps survive every stage, a record failing its quality gate is refused by name and never reaches the world model, a research-licensed dataset cannot be spent on a trade, written evidence cannot be revised, and every registry the platform acts on rebuilds byte-identically from the event log alone (one flipped byte refuses the replay).
